title: Client authentication bypass through premature DTLS 1.2 session caching
summary: The server cached a resumable session after ClientKeyExchange but before validating Finished and enforcing client authentication. An attacker can omit the certificate, leave the handshake unfinished, then resume using the master secret it knows. Requires a SessionStore, certificate-based cipher suite, and client-certificate requirement or rejecting VerifyConnection callback. WebRTC users are stated unaffected.
ai_role: The Pion maintainer's case-specific advisory credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier ANT-2026-8ECSI13S). It does not identify model versions or internal discovery dates.
classification_note: The cited advisory documents public disclosure; it does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The advisory identifies fix commit ce84b97 and the following package-version scope: v2 2.1.0–2.2.12 (no patched v2 version listed); v3 before 3.1.14, fixed 3.1.14. This source does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: unauthenticated remote client-authentication bypass on the described server configuration.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible attack path but does not report observed exploitation.
